questions.question: Why does a uniform review percentage (e.g. review 10% of everything) fail in practice?
options: It wastes reviewer time on low-risk types while under-reviewing high-risk ones
10% is always statistically insignificant regardless of context
Uniform percentages are illegal under data protection regulations
It requires more reviewers than any team can staff

questions.question: What two factors define 'risk' in risk-based human review allocation?
options: Document length and file format
The consequence of an error and the likelihood of an error
Processing cost and processing time
Model confidence alone, nothing else

questions.question: What review pattern should apply to the highest-risk document categories (e.g. payment instructions, legal documents)?
options: A small stratified sample, same as low-risk categories
100% human review regardless of the reported confidence score
No review at all, since they are processed too rarely to matter
Review only when confidence drops below 50%

questions.question: Within the set of items actually selected for review, what determines which gets reviewed first?
options: Strict first-in-first-out order, regardless of confidence
Alphabetical order by document name
Dynamic queue-based prioritization favoring lowest confidence / worst historical accuracy for that stratum
Random shuffling to ensure fairness across reviewers

questions.question: How do confidence calibration and stratified sampling feed into risk-based review allocation?
options: They are unrelated processes that happen independently
Calibration tells you what confidence really means, and sampling tells you if accuracy holds over time — review allocation turns those signals into a staffing decision
Risk-based review replaces the need for both calibration and sampling
Only stratified sampling matters; calibration has no bearing on review allocation

questions.question: Why does an all-or-nothing review split (fully automate some types, fully manual-review others) fall short?
options: It's more expensive than reviewing everything manually
It ignores per-extraction confidence variation within a type and doesn't adapt as accuracy changes over time
It requires more computing power than risk-based allocation
It's not compatible with schema validation
